lessons.title: खाना खाकर (khānā khākar) — one action, then the next
lessons.gloss: having eaten — joining one action to the next in a story, and after doing

segments.text: You met -कर with देखकर and करके: मैं किताब देखकर आता हूँ, "I'll look at the book and come". Say it once. Then "she came". (vah āī.)
This lesson takes -कर into the past, where stories are told.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: -कर in a story

segments.text: मैंने हाथ धोकर खाना खाया। maiṁne hāth dhokar khānā khāyā. — "I washed my hands and ate."
One doer, two actions, in the order they happened. The first drops its -ना and takes -कर; only the last verb carries the past. करना still gives करके.

The last verb decides ने. If it takes a thing, the doer takes ने: मैंने हाथ धोकर खाना खाया. If it does not, there is no ने, though something was eaten on the way: मैं खाना खाकर सो गया (maiṁ khānā khākar so gayā), "I ate and fell asleep".
वह सुबह उठकर नहाया। (vah subah uṭhkar nahāyā.) — He got up in the morning and bathed.
मीरा ने घर आकर चाय पी। (Mīrā ne ghar ākar cāy pī.) — Mira came home and drank tea.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: after doing

segments.text: नाश्ते के बाद हम बाज़ार गए। nāśte ke bād ham bāzār gae. — "After breakfast we went to the market."
के बाद, "after", follows a noun in its oblique form: नाश्ते के बाद. It follows a verb too, as के लिए does in करने के लिए: the -ना becomes -ने.
खाना खाने के बाद (khānā khāne ke bād) — after eating.
काम करने के बाद मैं घर आया। (kām karne ke bād maiṁ ghar āyā.) — After work I came home.
-कर needs one doer for both actions. When the doers differ, tell it in two sentences, or with जब … तब ….

segments.instruction: "I washed my hands and ate" — maiṁne hāth dhokar khānā khāyā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I washed my hands and ate" — *maiṁne hāth dhokar khānā khāyā*]

segments.instruction: "Mira came home and drank tea" — Mīrā ne ghar ākar cāy pī
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Mira came home and drank tea" — *Mīrā ne ghar ākar cāy pī*]

segments.prompt: Say that you got up and bathed, then that after breakfast you went to the market.
acceptedResponses: maiṁ uṭhkar nahāyā; nāśte ke bād maiṁ bāzār gayā
मैं उठकर नहाया। नाश्ते के बाद मैं बाज़ार गया।
मैं उठकर नहाई। नाश्ते के बाद मैं बाज़ार गई।
maiṁ uṭhkar nahāī; nāśte ke bād maiṁ bāzār gaī

feedback.correct: uṭhkar joins the first action to the second; nāśte ke bād puts breakfast first.
feedback.incorrect: Drop -nā and add -kar to the first verb; a noun before ke bād takes its oblique: nāśte.

segments.text: How many verbs in a -कर sentence carry the past? (One: the last.) Which verb decides ने? (The last: मैंने हाथ धोकर खाना खाया, but मैं खाना खाकर (khānā khākar) सो गया.) "After breakfast"? (नाश्ते के बाद.) "After eating"? (खाना खाने के बाद.)

lessons.title: आख़िर (ākhir) — at last, in the end
lessons.gloss: at last, finally; in the end

segments.text: Before the new one: say "I ate and fell asleep". (maiṁ khānā khākar so gayā.) A story needs a word for its last step, and for a wait that ends.
आख़िर — ākhir — "at last, finally".
दो घंटे के बाद आख़िर ट्रेन आई। do ghaṇṭe ke bād ākhir ṭren āī. — "After two hours the train came at last."
With में it closes a story: आख़िर में (ākhir meṁ), "in the end".
आख़िर में हम घर पहुँचे। ākhir meṁ ham ghar pahũce. — "In the end we reached home."
आख़िर (ākhir) is usually traced to Arabic ākhir, "last, the end", which reached Hindi through Persian. Its ख़, with the dot below, is the letter Hindi writes in many words that came this way.

segments.instruction: "After two hours the train came at last" — do ghaṇṭe ke bād ākhir ṭren āī
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "After two hours the train came at last" — *do ghaṇṭe ke bād ākhir ṭren āī*]

segments.instruction: "In the end we reached home" — ākhir meṁ ham ghar pahũce
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "In the end we reached home" — *ākhir meṁ ham ghar pahũce*]

segments.text: What does आख़िर (ākhir) mean? ("At last, finally".) "In the end"? (आख़िर (ākhir) में.)

lessons.title: पहले … फिर … (pahle … phir …) — first, then, after that, in the end
lessons.gloss: first … then … — keeping the steps of a story in order, with after that and in the end

segments.text: You know पहले, "first, earlier", and फिर, "again, then". Say both. Then "in the end". (ākhir meṁ.)

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the order words

segments.text: पहले मैं स्टेशन गया, फिर मैंने टिकट लिया। pahle maiṁ sṭeśan gayā, phir maiṁne ṭikaṭ liyā. — "First I went to the station, then I bought a ticket."
A story marks its steps:

utterances: step: the first. the word: पहले (pahle).
step: the next. the word: फिर (phir).
step: the one after. the word: उसके बाद (uske bād).
step: the last. the word: आख़िर में (ākhir meṁ).

segments.text: Each one opens its sentence, and the verb after it is the plain past. टिकट is masculine, so लिया.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: उसके बाद

segments.text: उसके बाद is "after that": उस, the form वह takes before a postposition, as in उसका, then के बाद. इसके बाद (iske bād), "after this", is built the same way, on इस, the form यह takes before a postposition.
उसके बाद हम गाड़ी में बैठे। uske bād ham gāṛī meṁ baiṭhe. — "After that we got on the train."

segments.instruction: "First we ate, then we went to the market" — pahle hamne khānā khāyā, phir ham bāzār gae
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "First we ate, then we went to the market" — *pahle hamne khānā khāyā, phir ham bāzār gae*]

segments.instruction: "After that I went home" — uske bād maiṁ ghar gayā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "After that I went home" — *uske bād maiṁ ghar gayā*]

segments.prompt: Tell three steps: first you went to the station, after that you got on the train, and in the end you reached the village.
acceptedResponses: pahle maiṁ sṭeśan gayā, uske bād maiṁ gāṛī meṁ baiṭhā, ākhir meṁ maiṁ gā̃v pahũcā
पहले मैं स्टेशन गया, उसके बाद मैं गाड़ी में बैठा, आख़िर में मैं गाँव पहुँचा।
पहले मैं स्टेशन गई, उसके बाद मैं गाड़ी में बैठी, आख़िर में मैं गाँव पहुँची।

feedback.correct: pahle, uske bād, ākhir meṁ: each opens its step.
feedback.incorrect: Open each step with its word, then the plain past: pahle … gayā, uske bād … baiṭhā, ākhir meṁ … pahũcā.

segments.text: Which word opens the first step? (पहले.) The next? (फिर.) "After that"? (उसके बाद.) The last? (आख़िर (ākhir) में.) Which past follows them? (The plain past.)

lessons.title: (reading) — a summer holiday in the village
lessons.gloss: a holiday in the village, told in order

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: Eighty-nine words, every one met before. Mira is writing. She went to her village last summer, and she tells it in order.

पिछले साल गर्मी की छुट्टी में मैं अपने गाँव गई। मुझे गाँव बहुत पसंद है। पहले मैंने स्टेशन पर टिकट लिया। फिर मैं गाड़ी में बैठी। गाड़ी में मैं एक किताब पढ़ रही थी। अचानक तेज़ बारिश हुई। शाम को मैं गाँव पहुँची। वहाँ दादी खाना बना रही थीं। मैंने हाथ धोकर दादी के साथ खाना खाया। खाना खाने के बाद दादी ने मुझे एक कहानी सुनाई। उसके बाद मैं छत पर गई। आसमान में बहुत तारे थे। आख़िर (ākhir) में मैं थककर सो गई। वह दिन बहुत अच्छा था।.

segments.instruction: the passage once without stopping; do not translate
segments.source: [YOU READ: the passage once without stopping; do not translate]

segments.instruction: the passage again, and sort every past verb: a scene or an event
segments.source: [YOU READ: the passage again, and sort every past verb: a scene or an event]

segments.text: गई, बैठी and पहुँची end in -ई: Mira is a woman, and these verbs have no thing. मैंने टिकट लिया and मैंने … खाना खाया follow the thing, and टिकट and खाना are masculine. दादी ने मुझे एक कहानी सुनाई follows कहानी, which is feminine; मुझे is the one it was told to.
पढ़ रही थी and बना रही थीं are the scene. थीं, with the dot, is for the grandmother, said with respect. तेज़ बारिश is heavy rain: तेज़ is "fast, sharp", and rain can be sharp.

segments.text: Why is बना रही थीं in the scene form? (The cooking was going on when Mira arrived.) Which words keep the steps in order? (पहले, फिर, उसके बाद, आख़िर (ākhir) में.)

segments.text: "I ate and fell asleep"? (मैं खाना खाकर (khānā khākar) सो गया: no ने, because सो गया has no thing.) "After eating"? (खाना खाने के बाद.) "After that"? (उसके बाद.) "At last"? (आख़िर (ākhir).) Who told Mira a story, and why सुनाई? (Her grandmother: दादी ने … कहानी सुनाई, and कहानी is feminine.)
